title: Space, gravity and quantum features are generic across many candidate rules

fields.label: Label
fields.value: Space, gravity and quantum features are generic across many candidate rules

fields.label: Statement
fields.value: Features such as seemingly continuous space and certain aspects of gravitation and quantum mechanics will emerge from many different underlying rules for the universe, whereas properties like the spectrum of particle masses, and perhaps the dimensionality of space, will be specific to particular rules.

fields.label: Quotation
fields.value: so also I suspect that properties such as the existence of seemingly continuous space, as well as certain features of gravitation and quantum mechanics, will emerge with many different possible underlying rules for the universe.

fields.label: Agent
fields.value: delphisci A New Kind of Science claim extractor

fields.label: Assumptions
fields.value: Stephen Wolfram, A New Kind of Science (Champaign, IL: Wolfram Media, 2002), Chapter 9, “Fundamental Physics”; section “Ultimate Models for the Universe” (from p. 465), p. 469. Scope: candidate fundamental rules for the universe

fields.label: Assessment
fields.value: GPT-5.6 Sol on wolfram2002-ch09-10: partially-resolvable, resolvability 0.43

fields.label: Finding
fields.value: Public rules and software permit tests on selected ensembles. They cannot establish genericity across the open-ended class of possible underlying rules, and resemblance to known physics may not discriminate genuine emergence.

fields.label: Proposed test in the assessment
fields.value: Proposed test with existing data: Define an ensemble of candidate rules and quantitative tests for continuum geometry, gravity-like dynamics, quantum behavior, dimension, and mass spectra, then estimate how frequently each property emerges. High prevalence of the first group but concentration of the second in rare rules would support the claim.

fields.label: Evidence against
fields.value:
No canonical distribution over candidate rules.

Existing searches cover a tiny subset of possible rules.

Emergence criteria are theory-laden.

fields.label: Dimension scores

data adequacy: 0.28

analysis feasibility: 0.35

fields.label: Finding
fields.value: The contrast between generic and rule-specific features is meaningful once a rule class is fixed, and it would be settled by enumeration rather than by new laboratory measurements. Published rule explorations are a small, self-selected sample and do not score gravitation, quantum features, and mass spectra side by side. The necessary computational survey does not exist.

fields.label: Proposed test in the assessment
fields.value: Proposed test with existing data: Fix a class of candidate universe rules, enumerate a large sample, and score which of continuous space, gravitational and quantum features, particle-mass ratios, and spatial dimension appear. The claim is supported if the first group recurs across many rules while mass ratios and dimension stay rule-specific; it is refuted if those 'generic' features are as rare as the mass spectrum.

fields.label: Evidence against
fields.value:
A survey large enough to separate generic from rule-specific features is far beyond a weeks-scale computation.

There is no agreed enumerable class of candidate rules for the universe.
